channel.title: Comments on: 88% never use personalization
channel.description: Instant Usability & Web Standards — static archive

item.title: By: Justin Lim
item.dc:creator: Justin Lim
item.description: data after data have always shown that personalization is not worth it. its funny how we keep spending $$ on personalization. Like technology convergence, personalization is one of those mythical ideas that we all wish or are convince that work but actually don’t.

item.title: By: Jonas
item.dc:creator: Jonas
item.description:
In a Swedish company with 6000 people, that a colleague of mine worked with, just under 100 had done any personalization whatsoeveron their intranet. That’s just over 1 percent – meaning that more than 98 percent didn’t do it.

100 persons was, coincidentally, about the number of people employed in the IT department.

item.title: By: Thomas Baekdal
item.dc:creator: Thomas Baekdal
item.description:
Very interesting research!

About a year ago we changed a part of our intranet at work. Before it allowed people to make their own versions/list etc. but the new version did not include this feature – why? because only 0.6% ever did so.
